RFC6286-2.1-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor) after d667673f7e; supersedes the pending rejudge-rfc6286.json. Row is {partial}. Tested: 'non-zero integer'. Gap: 'is the same for every local interface and every BGP peer', an owner-approved deviation (spec-bgp-open-session-rfc-defects Q2, 2026-10-13): the per-peer session router-id override read by Producer internal/component/bgp/reactor/config.go::parsePeerSettings gives a peer an identifier different from the others'; not counted conformant. Within Tested: config_test.go::TestParsePeerFromTreeInvalid zero_router_id_rejected requires a peer-level 0.0.0.0 to be refused with the RFC 6286 Section 2.1 error; rfc6286_router_id_test.go::TestRFC6286GlobalZeroRouterIDRejected requires PeersFromTree to refuse a global bgp router-id of 0.0.0.0 with that error and to accept 0.0.0.1, inherited by an override-less peer as identifier 1; TestRFC6286NonZeroRouterIDAccepted requires a peer-level 0.0.0.1 to become identifier 1. Auditor overlay mutants, all red: removing the zero check in parseRouterID (both zero negatives), bypassing parseRouterID in GlobalsFromTree only (the global-leaf test alone), widening the check to id < 2 (both 0.0.0.1 positives). Limit: a config with no router-id at either level reaches PeersFromTree as identifier 0; only the config mandatory check (validate_mandatory_bgp.go) refuses it, and no test tagged to this row exercises that path.

RFC6286-2.1-2.note: {single-polarity: positive} valid: lowercase should, the duplicate is the operator's allow-shared-router-id opt-out. Both halves of 'unique within an AS' now covered: remote peers by TestRouterIDClaimConcurrentOnlyOneWins (accepted == 1, routerIDConflictError); this speaker's own identifier by TestRFC6286LocalIdentifierUniqueWithinItsAS, which presents the local identifier 0x01020301 from an internal peer (AS 65001 both sides) on handleOpen and requires ErrBadBGPIdentifier, NOTIFICATION 2/3 on the wire and no OpenConfirm. Producer read: Open.ValidateBGPIdentifier (internal && id == localID). Judge break (overlay, open.go: the self check gated on !internal) turned the new unit red, the remote-peer unit green. Revert record on ValidateBGPIdentifier for the new unit; the HEAD unit still carries no record (proof by reading: the exact accepted == 1 assertion).

RFC6286-2.2-1.note: (a) accepting an OPEN whose BGP Identifier is zero; (b) TestOpenValidateBGPIdentifier: zero from internal and from external wantErr with NotifyOpenMessage / NotifyOpenBadBGPID; negative: 1 and 0xFFFFFFFF accepted. The same unit also proves the sentence's second clause (local id from internal rejected, from external accepted). handleOpen and processOpen rails tagged positive too.

RFC6286-2.2-2.note: (a) accepting the local identifier from an internal peer, or rejecting it from an external one; (b) TestOpenValidateBGPIdentifier rows 'local identifier from internal peer' wantErr 2/3 and 'from external peer' no error, plus localID+-1 accepted; zero rows cover the first clause. TestHandleOpenRejectsBadBGPIdentifier repeats both polarities on the FSM rail.

RFC6286-2.3-1.note: (a) with identical identifiers, preserving the connection of the smaller AS; (b) TestDetectCollisionEqualIdentifierPrefersLargerAS asserts accept/close for peer AS > local AS and peer AS < local AS with equal identifiers; negative rows show unequal identifiers ignore the AS.
